messages:
sam: Quick RFC follow-up — thinking about exposing a lightweight 'queue slice' view on the scheduler API so higher layers can make smarter admission/backpressure decisions.
sam: Right now the scheduler only exposes per-lane qlen and head latency; that hides per-slice token density and request urgency which is causing noisy flushes.
jin: Can you sketch what "queue slice" means in practice? is it per-model, per-tenant, or per-batch-key?
anika: My take: slice = (model, qos_tier, affinity_key). Small surface: counts, oldest_request_ts, estimated_tokens, stalled_flag.
leo: Tradeoff: more visibility -> more contention on the scheduler metadata and more frequent polls from control plane. Need bounded update frequency.
sam: Exactly. Proposal A: push-based deltas on significant changes (thresholded). Proposal B: pull-based snapshot per N ms. A is chatty for noisy workloads; B can be stale and cause bad admission.
jin: Also need to consider accuracy vs. cost for estimated_tokens. Do we use request.headers.token_estimate or compute from prompt length?
anika: Use client estimate + small 10% fudge; computing exact tokenization in scheduler is expensive and leaks per-request CPU.
leo: Another axis: expose a short-lifetime lease for a slice so orchestration can reserve capacity for canary rollouts or heavy requests. But leases complicate eviction logic.
sam: Example minimal interface (pseudo):
```
GET /scheduler/v1/slices?model=redwood-2
=> [{"slice_id":"m1-qos0-a:12","count":12,"est_tokens":3400,"oldest":1715000000,"lease_avail":true}]
```
jin: Looks fine, but consider backpressure signals too: e.g., 'drain_recommendation': "slow-path|reject|accept-if-lease".
ops-bot: SLO note: exposing stale slice counts can mislead autoscaler. If snapshot is 100ms stale we might overcommit and blow latency SLO for tail.
sam: Good call. We should mark each snapshot with 'observed_at' and 'uncertainty' bucket.
leo: Implementation pattern we've used: per-worker fast-path counters updated with relaxed atomics + worker local coalescer that publishes deltas every 50ms. That keeps contention low.
anika: For API-level ergonomics, clients should be able to subscribe to slice events (ws/stream) for realtime dashboards, but default to polling.
jin: How about security/data isolation for private deployments? slices may reveal tenant activity. Need RBAC and masking (aggregate-only) for non-admins.
sam: Yep — two modes: admin (full slice ids + counts) and tenant (only tenant's slices). Also opt-in telemetry for external partners.
leo: Performance tests to run: 1) high cardinality slices (many affinity keys) 2) bursty arrivals with small token estimates 3) steady large-token requests. Measure CPU, memory for metadata + percent of requests misrouted due to stale view.
anika: For rollout plan: start internal opt-in flag, collect metrics for 2 weeks, then default on for hosted. Private customers get toggle.
sam: Final ask: who can prototype a thin HTTP endpoint that returns per-worker aggregated slice snapshots (no tokenization) in next sprint? ping me if you can take it.
leo: I'll pair with jin on the prototype. expect an initial PR by EOW. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: feature/queue-slice-proto -> staging at 2024-09-12T02:00Z
jin: I'll mock client usage and add a small e2e that asserts no more than 5% extra CPU on workers.
ops-bot: Add a dashboard card for 'slice_delta_rps' and 'slice_snapshot_age_ms' before enabling global rollout.
sam: Awesome, thanks. Saving notes to the RFC thread. If anyone spots a missing tradeoff shout now.
